name: Longon
description: A coffin carved from a single log, recorded among sixteenth-century Visayans.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994)
Boxer Codex (c. 1590), Lilly Library, Indiana University

lore.en: Scott describes how sixteenth-century Visayans laid their honored dead in a longon, a coffin hollowed from a single tree trunk with a fitted lid. Some were carved and some were boat-shaped. The dead were dressed and given belongings, and the coffin was kept near the house or placed in a cave. Spanish writers recorded these customs in the years after contact.
lore.fil: Inilalarawan ni Scott kung paano inihihimlay ng mga Bisaya noong ika-16 na siglo ang kanilang pinarangalang patay sa longon, isang kabaong na inukit mula sa iisang puno na may takip. May mga inukitan at may hugis-bangka. Binibihisan ang patay at binibigyan ng mga gamit, at iniingatan ang kabaong malapit sa bahay o inilalagay sa kuweba. Naitala ng mga manunulat na Espanyol ang mga kaugaliang ito pagkaraan ng pagdating nila.

inGame.en: With the Visayan tradition, the Libingan keeps longon coffins. It speeds the barangay's recovery from mourning.
inGame.fil: Sa tradisyong Bisaya, mga longon ang nasa Libingan. Pinabibilis nito ang paggaling ng barangay mula sa pagluluksa.

hint.en: A resting place in the Visayan way.
